item.title: Latin America and Caribbean: Women Leaders With a Plan to Revive Multilateralism
item.description: In Montevideo recently, Latin America and the Caribbean did something the United Nations system has not seen in decades: Present a regionally diverse slate of secretary‑general candidates — including three women — participating in a debate and ready to redefine the future of multilateralism. The multilateral system is living through one of its most fragile ... Read more

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Spotlight on Israeli settler violence in West Bank
item.description: The Security Council holds an open debate on Tuesday which is expected to address escalating Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank as attacks on Palestinians and their property continue. UN News app users can follow here.

item.title: Colombia earthquake: International teams standing by
item.description: As earthquake rescue efforts across western Colombia continued on Tuesday, UN agencies said that they stood ready to help “with everything we've got” if and when the request came from the authorities for international assistance.

item.title: Myanmar: UN investigators document deliberate military attacks on civilians
item.description: Myanmar's military has carried out a sustained campaign of deliberate attacks on civilians – including airstrikes on homes, schools and camps for displaced people, alongside arbitrary detention, torture and sexual violence – according to Human Rights Council-appointed investigators.

item.title: World marks second warmest July on record
item.description: As multiple regions contend with unbearable heat, drought, wildfires and other extreme weather, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) on Tuesday underlined the crucial need for stronger forecasts and early warning systems to protect lives and livelihoods.

item.title: Ebola deaths top 2,000 as scientists race to develop vaccine
item.description: Local officials in the DR Congo (DRC) reported on Tuesday that deaths from the Ebola virus disease have surpassed 2,000, with half of that number in the last 20 days.

item.title: After post-pandemic improvement, youth unemployment is rising again
item.description: Frustrated by skyrocketing youth unemployment, among other issues, tens of thousands of Gen Z activists took to the streets of Nepal last year, demanding a stake in the country’s economic growth. The protest worked and the prime minister resigned.

item.title: South Sudan: UN mission decries deadly attacks, works to calm tensions after ‘nothing but devastation’
item.description: The UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) has condemned recent armed group attacks in Warrap state which reportedly left more than 60 civilians dead and 50 others injured.

item.title: Obstetric Violence: Syrian Women Speak Out
item.description: The abuse 30-year-old Nour Al-Badawi experienced in an Aleppo public hospital while giving birth resulted in her having two major follow-up operations and left her with depression and anxiety.
